newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique declares emergency in flood-hit areas.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique declares emergency in flood-hit areas.

text.p: Mozambique's government has declared emergency in four flood-hit provinces and appealed for foreign aid to help resettle thousands of people displaced by the floods, officials said on Wednesday.

"The Council of Ministers, meeting on Tuesday, considered the present flood situation in the provinces of Manica, Sofala, Tete and Zambezia as an emergency," a cabinet statement said after a meeting headed by President Joaquim Chissano.
It did not give details of the aid needed.

A government official told Reuters ministers at the meeting assessed relief operations already underway, additional funding needed for rescue operations, relief goods and resettlement of families affected by the floods.
At least 4,000 families lost their homes in areas around the flooded Zambezi, Pungue and Buzi rivers.
Crop losses, especially of the staple maize, are expected to be high.
Mozambique's second largest city, Beira, has been cut off from the rest of the country since last week, and prices of basic items such as maize, vegetables and charcoal in the city have soared.
Beira is directly affected by the Pungue and Buzi rivers.

Water levels on the Zambezi river are on the rise after the sluice gates of the country's biggest dam, the Cahora Bassa, were opened on Tuesday releasing up to 2,200 cubic metres of water every minute.
The South African Air Force, helping to evacuate flood victims in Mozambique, appealed to people living close to the river's banks to clear the area as water levels were expected to rise further.
The air force has helped to airlift more than 650 people threatened by floodwaters.
